inputs.original_text: It is deeply telling how the dominant political and academic establishments consistently choose to ignore the foundational human rights and structural injustices at play, instead falling back on militaristic rhetoric that completely disregards the safety and survival of vulnerable populations. When we look at the discourse coming from institutional defenders of the status quo, we see an alarming dismissal of civilian protection in favor of uncritical alignment and brute force. This persistent refusal to engage with the ethical realities of violence and oppression only perpetuates cycles of harm on the ground, silencing those who demand accountability, restraint, and a fundamental rethinking of foreign policy through a lens of human dignity and global justice.
inputs.modified_text:
Look, it is painfully obvious what is happening here when you examine how our political and academic institutions operate. They consistently choose to ignore the foundational human rights and structural injustices at play, relying instead on militaristic rhetoric that completely disregards the safety and survival of vulnerable populations. 

When we look at the discourse coming from institutional defenders of the status quo, we see an alarming dismissal of civilian protection in favor of uncritical alignment and brute force. This is entirely about preserving systemic power and oppression. Their persistent refusal to engage with the ethical realities of violence and oppression only perpetuates cycles of harm on the ground, actively silencing those who demand accountability, restraint, and a fundamental rethinking of foreign policy through a lens of human dignity and global justice. We cannot reform these broken systems without completely confronting the elites who protect them.
